Definition: from G3956 and a derivative of G4483; all out-spokenness, i.e. frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication, assurance:--bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly(-ness).
KeyPassages: John 16:25; Acts 4:13; Acts 4:29; Ephesians 3:12; Hebrews 4:16; John 18:20
BiblicalUsage: Parrhesia is boldness, openness, frankness, the freedom to speak plainly. The disciples speak with boldness in Acts 4:13 after the rulers see they are unlearned men, and Peter and John pray for boldness to speak the word in Acts 4:29 and 4:31, while Paul says in Ephesians 3:12 that in Christ we have boldness and access with confidence, and in Hebrews 4:16 believers are told to come boldly unto the throne of grace. Jesus speaks openly to the world in John 18:20, and promises in John 16:25 to speak plainly of the Father. The Greek text spells this word with a single rho after the prefix; the site's spelling doubles the rho, but it is the same noun.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe boldness is not a personality trait, it is a gift of the gospel: the unlearned speak plainly, the prisoners pray for more of it, and the throne of grace is approached without flinching. That is why I hold that the church that has lost its boldness has lost its voice, and the way back is the same as the way in, through Christ.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Simon Peter; John the Apostle; Paul
